The impact was catastrophic, causing a section of the bridge to succumb to gravity, sending it, along with up to 20 unfortunate souls, into the icy grip of the river below. As the sun rose, the river became a stage for a desperate search and rescue operation. Divers and teams worked tirelessly, combing the depths for signs of life and vehicles that had been dragged into the watery abyss, including one as sizable as a tractor trailer. The bridge, more than just a physical link, was a symbol of connectivity for the city, now broken. The incident prompted a swift response from Maryland's governor, Wes Moore, who declared a state of emergency. The coast guard, with a sense of urgency, deployed an array of response units, including boats and a helicopter, in a mission to find and rescue those affected. Amidst the chaos, efforts were made to establish contact with the operators of the Dali seeking to understand the sequence of events that led to this tragic moment. The response teams on the scene worked with precision and caution, ensuring the safety of all involved while striving to mitigate further harm. As the city grappled with the aftermath, Baltimore's mayor, Brandon Scott, took to the digital sphere in the early hours, announcing his journey to the scene where emergency personnel were already in action. The aftermath was captured in striking footage showing the bridge's collapse, a testament to the force of the collision. The resulting plumes of smoke and fire served as a grim reminder of the bridge's namesake, Francis Scott Key, who once witnessed a historic bombardment near this site, inspiring him to pen the Star Spangled Banner.
